rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun may refer to a human other than Adam, with an omitted possessive, or to Adam with his descendants intended; it may also refer to humanity as suited to descendants.
rows.anchor: فإن أريد غير آدم فواضح، ويكون خلقه من سلالة الطين خلق أصله وهو آدم

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī favors reading al-insān as apt to refer either to the origin or descendants, with each pronoun referring to what suits it.
rows.anchor: ويعود كل شيء لما يليق به. وإليه نحا الزمخشري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase may attach to jaʿalnāhu or be an omitted adjective of nuṭfah.
rows.anchor: يجوز أن يتعلق بالجعل، وأن يتعلق بمحذوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qarār is a place of settlement, here the womb; makīn describes its secure location, metaphorically like a road called travelling, or because it is firmly established in itself.
rows.anchor: والقرار: المستقر وهو موضع الاستقرار. والمراد بها الرحم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khalaqa here carries the transformational sense of jaʿala and therefore takes two objects; jaʿala can likewise carry the sense of creating and take one.
rows.anchor: التصييرية فتعدت لاثنين كما تضمن جعل معنى خلق فيتعدى لواحد

rows.speaker: العامة
rows.claim: The common reading has both ʿiẓām and al-ʿiẓām in the plural.
rows.anchor: قرأ العامة " عظاما " و " العظام " بالجمع فيهما

rows.speaker: ابن عامر وأبو بكر عن عاصم
rows.claim: Ibn ʿĀmir and Abū Bakr from ʿĀṣim read both occurrences in the singular.
rows.anchor: وابن عامر وأبو بكر عن عاصم " عظما " و " العظم " بالإفراد فيهما

rows.speaker: السلمي والأعرج والأعمش
rows.claim: Al-Sulamī, al-Aʿraj, and al-Aʿmash read the first occurrence singular and the second plural.
rows.anchor: والسلمي والأعرج والأعمش بإفراد الأول وجمع الثاني

rows.speaker: أبو رجاء ومجاهد وإبراهيم ابن أبي بكر
rows.claim: Abū Rajāʾ, Mujāhid, and Ibrāhīm ibn Abī Bakr read the first occurrence plural and the second singular.
rows.anchor: وأبو رجاء ومجاهد وإبراهيم ابن أبي بكر بجمع الأول وإفراد الثاني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Plural matches the intended many bones, while singular can denote a generic class, as in “my bone.”
rows.anchor: فالجمع على الأصل لأنه مطابق لما يراد به، والإفراد للجنس كقوله

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī explains singular-for-plural as unambiguous because a human has many bones.
rows.anchor: قال الزمخشري: " وضع الواحد موضع الجمع لزوال اللبس لأن الإنسان ذو عظام كثيرة "

rows.speaker: الشيخ
rows.claim: The grammarians of Sībawayh’s school allow singular for plural only by poetic necessity, citing a stomach in the singular although each person has one.
rows.anchor: هذا عند سيبويه وأصحابه لا يجوز إلا في ضرورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Poetry also uses singular ʿaẓm for plural throats, supporting singular-for-plural usage.
rows.anchor: في حلقكم عظم وقد شجينا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further poetic example uses singular jilduhā for the plural hides of the exhausted animals.
rows.anchor: به جيف الحسرى فأما عظامها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qurʾānic singular samʿ likewise exemplifies a singular noun used generically for plural hearing.
rows.anchor: وقد تقدم طرف من هذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aḥsanu al-khāliqīn may be apposition to the divine name, an adjective—which is preferable because derived-form apposition is uncommon—or a predicate with an omitted subject, though ellipsis is less likely.
rows.anchor: أحدها: أنه بدل من الجلالة. الثاني: أنه نعت للجلالة وهو أولى مما قبله

rows.speaker: أبو البقاء
rows.claim: Abū al-Baqāʾ rejects the adjective parse because the superlative remains indefinite even when annexed to a definite noun.
rows.anchor: وقد منع أبو البقاء أن يكون وصفا قال: " لأنه نكرة وإن أضيف لمعرفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author answers that Abū al-Baqāʾ relies on one disputed account of superlative annexation; the correct account treats it as a genuine definite annexation.
rows.anchor: وهذا بناء منه على أحد القولين في أفعل التفضيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-khāliqīn means those who estimate or determine; Zuhayr’s line uses khalaqta in that sense.
rows.anchor: والخالقين أي: المقدرين كقول زهير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The comparison’s distinguishing measure is omitted but understood from the annexed noun: best in creation or estimation, just as the object of permission is understood from its relative clause.
rows.anchor: والمميز لأفعل محذوف لدلالة المضاف إليه عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Talfaḥu may begin an independent sentence, function circumstantially, or serve as another predicate of ulāʾika.
rows.anchor: يجوز استئنافه، ويجوز حاليته. ويجوز كونه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lafḥ is the fire striking, scorching, and burning something, more severe than nafḥ.
rows.anchor: إصابة النار الشيء/ وكلحها وإحراقها له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kulūḥ is the upper lip drawn up and the lower lip slackened; the cited al-Tirmidhī report describes them stretching to the head’s middle and navel.
rows.anchor: وفي الترمذي: تتقلص شفته العليا، حتى تبلغ وسط رأسه، وتسترخي السفلى حتى تبلغ سرته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The expression “a lion’s kulūḥ” denotes baring its teeth; a harsh day or cold is also called kāliḥ.
rows.anchor: أي: تكشيره عن أنيابه. ودهر كالح، وبرد كالح

rows.speaker: غير مسمى
rows.claim: Another explanation takes kulūḥ as a frowning, grimacing face.
rows.anchor: وقيل: الكلوح هو: تقطيب الوجه وبسوره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Istīʾnās can mean relieving the visitor’s unease about whether permission will be granted, and thus serves as a synonym for seeking permission.
rows.anchor: لأن الطارق يستوحش من أنه: هل يؤذن له أو لا؟ فيزال استيحاشه

rows.speaker: غير مسمى
rows.claim: An alternative derives the word from seeing or perceiving, meaning to ascertain the situation before entering.
rows.anchor: وقيل: من الإيناس وهو الإبصار أي: حتى تستكشفوا الحال

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glossed the expression as “until you seek permission”; this is an explanatory gloss, not a reading.
rows.anchor: وفسره ابن عباس " حتى تستأذنوا " وليست قراءة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The claim attributed to Ibn ʿAbbās that the written form was a scribal mistake for tastaʾdhinū is fabricated against him.
rows.anchor: وما ينقل عنه أنه قال: " تستأنسوا خطأ من الكاتب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question resembles the earlier discussion of yaʾs in “Have the believers not despaired?”
rows.anchor: وهو نظير ما تقدم في الرعد أفلم ييأس الذين آمنوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Istīʾnās can mean seeking information; the cited verse of poetry uses mustaʾnis for an observer keeping watch.
rows.anchor: 3440 كأن رحلي وقد زال النهار بنا

rows.speaker: غير مسمى
rows.claim: A further derivation connects the word to al-uns: ascertain whether anyone is inside.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هو من الإنس بكسر الهمزة أي: يتعرف

rows.speaker: الطبري
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabarī relates the explanation “make yourselves feel at ease.”
rows.anchor: وحكى الطبري أنه بمعنى: وتؤنسوا أنفسكم

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya says the verb’s morphology rules out deriving it from ānasa.
rows.anchor: تصريف الفعل يأبى أن يكون من آنس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In yakhiḏūnaka is negative; huzuwan is the second object, either a place of mockery or someone mocked.
rows.anchor: مفعول ثان، ويحتمل أن يكون التقدير: موضع هزء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The negative clause can answer the conditional; after iḏā, a negative answer with mā, in, or lā needs no faʾ.
rows.anchor: أنها جواب الشرطية. واختصت " إذا " بأن جوابها متى كان منفيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On that parse, an implicit saying governs the quoted question, and that saying is circumstantial: they mock him while saying this.
rows.anchor: يكون قوله: " أهذا الذي " في محل نصب بالقول المضمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the negative clause interrupts between iḏā and its answer; the answer is the implied statement quoted by a-hādhā.
rows.anchor: أنها جملة معترضة بين " إذا " وجوابها، وجوابها: هو ذلك القول المضمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The object of baʿatha is omitted and refers back to the relative pronoun.
rows.anchor: ومفعول " بعث " محذوف هو عائد الموصول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rasūlan is normally an adjective functioning as a circumstantial accusative; treating it as a verbal noun for “message” requires an omitted muḍāf or an intensive or passive-agent sense, which the author calls strained.
rows.anchor: " رسولا " على بابه من كونه صفة فينتصب على الحال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two objects of ittakhadha remain in their stated order because both are equally definite.
rows.anchor: مفعولا الاتخاذ من غير تقديم ولا تأخير لاستوائهما في التعريف

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī says hawāhu is advanced for emphasis, comparing it to “I knew Zayd as departing.”
rows.anchor: ما هو إلا تقديم المفعول الثاني على الأول للعناية به

rows.speaker: الشيخ
rows.claim: The Shaykh objects that calling this inversion is improper because such inversion belongs to poetic necessity.
rows.anchor: وادعاء القلب يعني التقديم ليس بجيد لأنه من ضرائر الأشعار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author rejects that objection: this is merely preposing and postposing, not the disputed poetic “inversion.”
rows.anchor: على أن هذا ليس من القلب المذكور في شيء، إنما هو تقديم وتأخير فقط

rows.speaker: ابن هرمز
rows.claim: Ibn Hurmuz reads ilāhata hawāhu on the faʿāla pattern; ilāhah means the worshiped one, with an intensive hāʾ, and is the indefinite second object placed first.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن هرمز " إلاهة هواه " على وزن فعالة. والإهة بمعنى

rows.speaker: غير مسمى
rows.claim: Some explain ilāhah here as the sun; the author objects that a proper feminine name should be diptote, while the counterargument says it often takes al- and becomes an indefinite adjective when stripped of it.
rows.anchor: وقيل: الإهة هي الشمس. ورد هذا: بأنه كان ينبغي أن يمتنع من الصرف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The name for the sun is also attested as alāhah, with ḍamma on the initial hamza.
rows.anchor: ويقال: ألاهة بضم الهمزة أيضا اسما للشمس

rows.speaker: بعض المدنيين
rows.claim: Some Medinans read ālihatan hawāhu, a preposed plural second object, treating the worshiped gods as different kinds.
rows.anchor: وقرأ بعض المدنيين " آلهة هواه " جمع إله، وهو أيضا مفعول مقدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first object of araʾayta is man, and its second object is the interrogative clause.
rows.anchor: ومفعول " أرأيت " الأول " من " ، والثاني: الجملة الاستفهامية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kam is a multiplicative exclamatory/interrogative of abundance, governed as a direct object by the following verb; min kulli zawjin is its specification.
rows.anchor: فهي خبرية، وهي منصوبة بما بعدها على المفعول به

rows.speaker: أبو البقاء
rows.claim: Abū al-Baqāʾ allows min kulli zawjin to be circumstantial, a parse the author says has no point.
rows.anchor: وجوز أبو البقاء أن يكون حالا ولا معنى له

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī explains that kull gives detailed comprehensiveness over plant kinds, while kam emphasizes that this total is exceedingly numerous.
rows.anchor: قد دل " كل " على الإحاطة بأزواج النبات على سبيل التفصيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The governing verb for iḏ is implicit: al-Zajjāj estimates “recite,” while others estimate “remember.”
rows.anchor: العام فيه مضمر. فقدره الزجاج: اتل، وغيره: اذكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An can be explanatory or a masdariyya particle, equivalent here to “that you come.”
rows.anchor: يجوز أن تكون مفسرة، وأن تكون مصدرية أي بأن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qawma Firʿawn is apposition or explicative apposition to al-qawm al-ẓālimīn.
rows.anchor: بدل أو عطف بيان للقوم الظالمين

rows.speaker: أبو البقاء
rows.claim: Abū al-Baqāʾ parses qawma Firʿawn as the object of tattaqūn in the address reading, or as a vocative.
rows.anchor: إنه مفعول " تتقون " على قراءة من قرأ " تتقون "

rows.speaker: العامة
rows.claim: The common reading uses third-person yattaqūna with an open n; the people of Pharaoh are meant and “punishment” is the omitted object.
rows.anchor: العامة على الياء في " يتقون " وفتح النون، والمراد قوم فرعون

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن مسلم ابن يسار وحماد وشقيق بن سلمة
rows.claim: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muslim ibn Yasār, Ḥammād, and Shaqīq ibn Salama read with second-person tāʾ, shifting address to rebuke them.
rows.anchor: قرأ عبد الله بن مسلم ابن يسار وحماد وشقيق بن سلمة بالتاء من فوق

rows.speaker: غير مسمى
rows.claim: Another reading has third-person yaʾ and a kasra on n; this may be a present verb whose first-person object yāʾ is represented by the kasra.
rows.anchor: وقرأ بعضهم " يتقون " بالياء من تحت وكسر النون. وفيها تخريجان

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī also parses it as yāʾ of address followed by the imperative ittaqūn, “O people, fear Me”; the author calls this remote.
rows.anchor: جوزه الزمخشري أن تكون " يا " للنداء. و " اتقون " فعل أمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sentence can stand independently; al-Zamakhsharī also allows a circumstantial clause describing the wrongdoers as not fearing God or His punishment.
rows.anchor: وفي هذه الجملة وجهان، أحدهما: أنها مستأنفة لا محل لها من الإعراب

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī treats the clause as circumstantial from the pronoun in al-ẓālimīn; the Shaykh objects that qawma Firʿawn intervenes and that a pre-hamza element cannot govern what follows it.
rows.anchor: وجوز الزمخشري أن تكون حالا من الضمير في الظالمين أي: يظلمون غير متقين

rows.speaker: الشيخ
rows.claim: The Shaykh gives two syntactic objections to the circumstantial parse: an intervening unrelated phrase and the rule that what follows the interrogative hamza cannot be governed from before it.
rows.anchor: خطأه الشيخ من وجهين، أحدهما: أنه يلزم منه الفصل بين الحال وعاملها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent force of alā is an offer or exhortation; al-Zamakhsharī takes it as lā with an interrogative of denial, while another view makes it an attention particle.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن " ألا " للعرض. وقال الزمخشري

rows.speaker: الشعبي
rows.claim: Al-Shaʿbī reads faʿlataka with kasra, meaning the manner or type of deed, namely the blow.
rows.anchor: وقرأ " فعلتك " بالكسر على الهيئة: الشعبي لأنها نوع من القتل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause anta mina al-kāfirīn may be circumstantial or an independent sentence.
rows.anchor: يجوز أن تكون حالا، وأن تكون مستأنفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb is feminine because qawm is grammatically feminine, as its diminutive quwayma shows, or because qawm means umma; the later pronoun is masculine by predominance of male members.
rows.anchor: إنما أنث فعل القوم؛ لأنه مؤنث بدليل تصغيره على قويمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The object of tattaqūn is omitted and understood as God’s punishment.
rows.anchor: وحذف مفعول " تتقون " أي: ألا تتقون عقاب الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural pronoun in ʿaṣawka may refer to the unbelievers disobeying the call to monotheism.
rows.anchor: أنها ضمير الكفار أي: فإن عصاك الكفار في أمرك لهم بالتوحيد

rows.speaker: غير مسمى
rows.claim: Another view takes the pronoun as the believers disobeying in subsidiary Islamic rulings after believing the Messenger; the author calls this extremely remote.
rows.anchor: أنها ضمير المؤمنين أي: فإن عصاك المؤمنون في فروع الإسلام وبعض الأحكام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author judges the interpretation that the pronoun refers to believers as extremely remote.
rows.anchor: وهذا في غاية البعد

rows.speaker: نافع وابن عامر
rows.claim: Nāfiʿ and Ibn ʿĀmir read fa-tawakkal; the faʾ makes the command a consequence of what precedes.
rows.anchor: قرأ نافع وابن عامر بالفاء. والباقون بالواو. فأما قراءة الفاء جعل فيها ما بعد الفاء

rows.speaker: الباقون
rows.claim: The other readers have wa-tawakkal, merely coordinating one sentence with another.
rows.anchor: وقراءة الواو لمجرد عطف جملة على أخرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alladhī yarāka may be nominative as predicate of an omitted subject, accusative as praise, or genitive as adjective, apposition, or explicative apposition.
rows.anchor: يجوز أن يكون مرفوع المحل خبرا لمبتدأ محذوف، أو منصوبه على المدح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the common reading taqallubaka is a noun coordinated with the object of yarāka: “and He sees your turning.”
rows.anchor: عطف على مفعول " يراك " أي: ويرى تقلبك

rows.speaker: جناح بن حبيش
rows.claim: Junāḥ ibn Ḥubaysh reads yuqallibuka as a verb with doubled lām, coordinated with yarāka: “the One who turns you.”
rows.anchor: وقرأ جناح بن حبيش بالياء من تحت مضمومة، وكسر اللام ورفع الباء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the passive subject of nūdiya is Mūsā, an may be explanatory, masdariyya with an omitted preposition, or lightened from anna with an implicit pronoun of شأن; as a prayer, bӯrika needs no separator.
rows.anchor: وهو الظاهر. وفي " أن " حينئذ ثلاثة أوجه

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī rejects lightened anna because he requires qad before the predicate and says it cannot be omitted as a particle; that assumes bӯrika is declarative, not a prayer.
rows.anchor: قال الزمخشري: " فإن قلت: هل يجوز أن تكون المخففة من الثقيلة، والتقدير: بأنه بورك. والضمير ضمير الشأن والقصة؟ قلت: لا لأنه لا بد من

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If bӯrika is a prayer as in the earlier discussion of 24:9, no separator is needed, though the author notes the difficulty that a request normally cannot be the predicate of lightened anna.
rows.anchor: أما إذا قلنا: إنه دعاء كما تقدم في النور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the whole phrase an bӯrika can be the passive subject, with a deleted preposition; an may be masdariyya or lightened.
rows.anchor: أن القائم مقام الفاعل نفس " أن بورك " على حذف حرف الجر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third analysis makes the passive subject an implicit verbal noun: “the call was called,” then explained by what follows, as in the story of Joseph.
rows.anchor: أنه ضمير المصدر المفهوم من الفعل أي: نودي النداء، ثم فسر بما بعده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Man fī al-nār is the passive subject of bӯrika; bāraka can take a direct object and occurs in several prepositional constructions, as the cited poems attest.
rows.anchor: " من " قائم مقام الفاعل ل " بورك ". وبارك يتعدى بنفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An unnamed poet attests bāraka with a direct object, and ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Zubayr attests it with fī.
rows.anchor: فبوركت مولودا وبوركت ناشئا وبوركت عند الشيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Zubayr’s poem witnesses the construction bӯrika fī.
rows.anchor:
وقال عبد الله بن الزبير:
3540 فبورك في بنيك وفي بنيهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further anonymous poem attests the same blessing verb with fī.
rows.anchor: بورك الميت الغريب كما بو

rows.speaker: غير مسمى
rows.claim: One view takes “those in the fire” as God, with an omitted muḍāf meaning His power and dominion in the fire.
rows.anchor: والمراد ب " من ": إما الباري تعالى، وهو على حذف مضاف

rows.speaker: غير مسمى
rows.claim: Another view identifies those in and around the fire as Mūsā and the angels.
rows.anchor: وقيل: المراد به موسى والملائكة، وكذلك بمن حولها

rows.speaker: غير مسمى
rows.claim: A further view takes man as nonrational things: the light and the surrounding places.
rows.anchor: وقيل: المراد ب " من " غير العقلاء وهو النور والأمكنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Subḥāna Allāh may continue the call, making both blessing and glorification the content of the summons.
rows.anchor: أنه من تتمة النداء أي: نودي بالبركة وتنزيه رب العزة

rows.speaker: غير مسمى
rows.claim: Another analysis treats it as God’s address to Muḥammad, an interruption within the narrative.
rows.anchor: أنه من كلام الله تعالى مخاطبا لنبينا محمد عليه الصلاة والسلام

rows.speaker: غير مسمى
rows.claim: A third interpretation expands the phrase as “blessed is whoever glorifies God,” omitting man and its relative clause; subḥān is governed by an omitted cognate verb, not qāla.
rows.anchor: يعني أنه حذف " من " وصلتها وأبقى معمول الصلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wa-alqi is coordinated with the preceding nominal declarative sentence; Sībawayh does not require coordinated sentences to share grammatical form.
rows.anchor: عطف على ما قبله من الجملة الاسمية الخبرية. وقد تقدم أن سيبويه لا يشترط تناسب الجمل

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī coordinates alqi with bӯrika, supplying “and it was said to him: throw your staff,” and supports it with the repeated explanatory an in the narrative.
rows.anchor: لأن المعنى: نودي أن بورك. وقيل له: ألق عصاك

rows.speaker: الشيخ
rows.claim: The Shaykh objects that al-Zamakhsharī’s cited innahu is itself coordinated with bӯrika, not the quoted command; the paraphrase requires an extra “it was said to him.”
rows.anchor: قال: الشيخ: " وقوله: " إنه معطوف على " بورك "

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author rejects requiring parallel sentence forms for coordination and supports Sībawayh’s allowance of nonparallel clauses.
rows.anchor: والصحيح أنه لا يشترط ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tahitazzu is circumstantial from the object pronoun in tarāhā, since the seeing is visual.
rows.anchor: جملة حالية من هاء " تراها " لأن الرؤية بصرية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kaʾannahā jānn may be a second circumstantial clause or a nested circumstantial clause from the pronoun in tahitazzu.
rows.anchor: يجوز أن تكون حالا ثانية، وأن تكون حالا من ضمير " تهتز "

rows.speaker: الحسن والزهري وعمرو بن عبيد
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan, al-Zuhrī, and ʿAmr ibn ʿUbayd read jāʾn with hamza in place of alif.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الحسن والزهري وعمرو بن عبيد " جأن " بهمزة مكان الألف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wa-lam yuʿaqqib may coordinate with wallā or be another circumstantial clause; it means he did not turn back.
rows.anchor: يجوز أن يكون عطفا على " ولى " ، وأن يكون حالا أخرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Poetry uses ʿaqqabū for turning back, attesting the sense “did not return on his tracks.”
rows.anchor: فما عقبوا إذ قيل: هل من معقب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hadiyya is something sent as a courtesy and names the gifted object; it could historically be a passive-participle noun, but is not a regular verbal noun of the form-four verb ahdā, whose masdar is ihdāʾ.
rows.anchor: والهدية: ما بعث على جهة الإكرام، وهي اسم للمهدى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fa-nāẓiratun coordinates with mursilatun; bi-ma is governed by yarjiʿu, with the interrogative fronted and the question suspending nāẓira.
rows.anchor: عطف على " مرسلة ". و " بم " متعلق ب " يرجع "

rows.speaker: الهوفي
rows.claim: Al-Ḥawfī mistakenly attaches bi-ma to nāẓira; the author says that fails because the interrogative must lead its clause.
rows.anchor: وقد وهم الحوفي فجعلها متعلقة ب " ناظرة " وهذا لا يستقيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The messenger is omitted after “when he came to Solomon,” implied by the Queen’s statement that she would send; it means the class of messengers, not one individual.
rows.anchor: أضمره لدلالة قولها " مرسلة " فإنه يستلزم رسولا. والمراد به الجنس

rows.speaker: عبد الله
rows.claim: ʿAbd Allāh reads jāʾū and later fa-irjiʿū, matching the plural messengers addressed by Solomon.
rows.anchor: ولذلك قرأ عبد الله " فلما جاؤوا " وقرأ " فارجعوا " إليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Atumiddūnan is an interrogative of rejection.
rows.anchor: استفهام إنكار. وقرأ حمزة بإدغام نون الرفع في نون الوقاية

rows.speaker: حمزة
rows.claim: Ḥamza assimilates the indicative nūn into the nūn of protection; the yāʾ is omitted in pause and retained in continuation.
rows.anchor: وقرأ حمزة بإدغام نون الرفع في نون الوقاية

rows.speaker: الباقون
rows.claim: The remaining readers retain two nūns; the yāʾ patterns vary: Nāfiʿ and Abū ʿAmr with Ḥamza, Ibn Kathīr in both positions, and the rest omit it in both.
rows.anchor: والباقون بنونين على الأصل. وأما الياء فإن نافعا وأبا عمرو كحمزة

rows.speaker: نافع
rows.claim: A reading transmitted from Nāfiʿ has one nūn, making three reading forms in all, comparable to the reading in al-Zumar.
rows.anchor: وروي عن نافع أنه يقرأ بنون واحدة، فتكملت ثلاث قراءات

words: فَمَآ ءَاتَىٰنِۦَ ٱللَّهُ خَيْرٌۭ مِّمَّآ ءَاتَىٰكُم
rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī says waw implies the addressees already know Solomon is richer but sent aid anyway, whereas faʾ suggests they did not know and are now told he needs no aid.
rows.anchor: إذا قلته بالواو فقد جعلت مخاطبي عالما بزيادتي عليه في الغنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author questions whether waw versus faʾ alone conveys that distinction and says al-Zamakhsharī also leaves unanswered why Solomon attributes wealth to God instead of saying he is richer.
rows.anchor: وفي هذا الفرق نظر؛ إذ لا يفهم ذلك بمجرد الواو والفاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Solomon credits God for his wealth to acknowledge the divine favor and avoid boasting.
rows.anchor: أنه أسند إيتاء الغنى إلى الله إظهارا لنعمته عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bal antum is a transition: after rejecting the offer and explaining the rejection, Solomon shifts to the motive—their delight in worldly gain, the only cause of satisfaction they recognize.
rows.anchor: إضراب انتقال. قال الزمخشري

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī notes that the annexation of “your gift” could refer either to its giver or its recipient.
rows.anchor: والهدية يجوز إضافته إلى المهدي. وإلى المهدى إليه وهي هنا محتملة للأمرين

rows.speaker: الشيخ
rows.claim: The Shaykh prefers annexation to the recipient; he also allows annexation to the giver, meaning they rejoice proudly in their gift.
rows.anchor: قال الشيخ: " وهي هنا مضافة للمهدى إليه. وهذا هو الظاهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author rejects the recipient as the apparent possessor: there is no report that Solomon sent them a gift, so the annexation must refer to the giver.
rows.anchor: لم ينقل أن سليمان صلى الله عليه وسلم أرسل إليهم هدية في هذه الحالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām may express figurative purpose, since the outcome is treated as the act’s motive, or result/consequence.
rows.anchor: في اللام الوجهان المشهوران: العلية المجازية بمعنى: أن ذلك لما كان نتيجة فعلهم

rows.speaker: العامة
rows.claim: The common reading has fatḥ on ḥāʾ and zāy; the two Hamza-and-Kisāʾī readings have ḍamma and sukūn, with both forms synonymous.
rows.anchor: وقرأ العامة بفتح الحاء والزاي وهي لغة قريش والأخوان بضم وسكون

rows.speaker: العامة
rows.claim: The common reading has hamza and derives from khaṭiʾa, error, the opposite of correctness.
rows.anchor: العامة على الهمز. مأخوذ من الخطأ ضد الصواب

rows.speaker: غير مسمى
rows.claim: A hamza-less yāʾ reading may be the same word softened, or derive from khaṭā yakhtū, “to step past” what is correct.
rows.anchor: وقرىء بياء دون همزة، فاحتمل أن يكون كالأول ولكن خفف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two pronouns in the clause apparently refer to Mūsā.
rows.anchor: الظاهر أن الضميرين لموسى

rows.speaker: غير مسمى
rows.claim: An alternative takes the pronouns as the Israelite and the Egyptian enemy; the Israelite, mistaking Mūsā’s movement as aggression, speaks, spreading the news while the killer remained uncertain.
rows.anchor: وقيل: للإسرائيلي والعدو هو القبطي. والضمير في " قال يا موسى " للإسرائيلي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An is regularly extra after lammā, as here, and before law when preceded by an oath.
rows.anchor: و " أن " تطرد زيادتها في موضعين، أحدهما: بعد " لما " كهذه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One cited poetic line attests extra an before wāw after an oath.
rows.anchor: أما والله أن و كنت حرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second poetic line attests extra an before law after an oath.
rows.anchor: فأقسم أن لو التقينا وأنتم

rows.speaker: العامة
rows.claim: The common reading has yibṭishu with kasra on the ṭāʾ.
rows.anchor: والعامة على " يبطش " بالكسر

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر
rows.claim: Abū Jaʿfar reads yabṭushu with ḍamma on the ṭāʾ.
rows.anchor: وضمها أبو جعفر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yasʿā may be an adjective or circumstantial clause because the indefinite man has been specified by “from the outskirts”; if min aqṣā attaches to jāʾa, it can only be an adjective.
rows.anchor: يجوز أن يكون صفة، وأن يكون حالا؛ لأن النكرة قد تخصصت

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī allows only the adjective parse if min aqṣā is attached to jāʾa, following the majority grammatical position.
rows.anchor: قاله الزمخشري، بناء منه على مذهب الجمهور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author notes Sībawayh allows the circumstantial parse without that restriction.
rows.anchor: أن سيبويه يجيز ذلك من غير شرط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase order differs from the man in 36:20: there he merely came from the far side, while here he is described as being from the outskirts; the two are different men and stories.
rows.anchor: وفي آية يس تقدم " من أقصى " على " رجل " لأنه لم يكن من أقصاها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yaʾtamirūn means they consult one another, as in al-Namir ibn Tawlab’s line using yuʾtamar.
rows.anchor: أرى الناس قد أحدثوا شيمة

rows.speaker: ابن قتيبة
rows.claim: Ibn Qutayba derives the meaning as people ordering one another, from the verse waʾtamirū baynakum bi-maʿrūf.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن قتيبة: يأمر بعضهم بعضا.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lak may attach to an implied “advisor for you,” to al-nāṣiḥīn through broad adverb usage, or serve as an explicative phrase.
rows.anchor: يجوز أن يتعلق بما يدل " الناصحين " عليه أي: ناصح لك من الناصحين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yataraqqabu means that Mūsā awaited guidance and God’s succor.
rows.anchor: أي: يترقب هدايته وغوث الله إياه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The response to law is omitted: either “when they saw the punishment” or “to repel it.”
rows.anchor: جوابها محذوف أي: لما رأوا العذاب أو لدفعوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mā is a relative pronoun meaning “that which”; its relative clause includes in and what follows, explaining the kasra on in.
rows.anchor: " ما " موصولة بمعنى الذي، صلتها " إن " وما في حيزها

rows.speaker: الأخفش الصغير
rows.claim: Al-Akhfash the Younger transmits that the Kufans prohibit a relative clause from beginning with in and consider it objectionable, despite its Qurʾānic occurrence.
rows.anchor: ونقل الأخفش الصغير عن الكوفيين منع الوصل ب " إن "

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One parse makes bāʾ causative like hamza, without inversion: the keys make the strong group stagger under their burden.
rows.anchor: أن الباء للتعدية كالهمزة، ولا قلب في الكلام. والمعنى: لتنيء المفاتيح العصبة الأقوياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nāʾa bi-shayʾ means to bear it with difficulty; Abū Zayd glosses nāʾtu bi-l-ʿamal as rising to undertake the work, supported by the cited poems.
rows.anchor: ومعنى ناء بكذا: نهض به بثقل

rows.speaker: أبو زيد
rows.claim: Abū Zayd explains nāʾtu bi-l-ʿamal as “I rose to carry out the work,” and poetry attests nāʾa with a load.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو زيد: " نؤت بالعمل أي: نهضت "

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī interprets nāʾa as making the load heavy and causing the carrier to lean; this yields the sense that the keys weigh down the group.
rows.anchor: وفسره الزمخشري بالإثقال. قال:

rows.speaker: أبو عبيد
rows.claim: Abū ʿUbayd proposes inversion: the group is the subject that bears the keys, as in saying a she-camel was presented to a watering trough.
rows.anchor: والثاني: أن في الكلام قلبا، والأصل: لتنوء العصبة بالمفاتح، أي: لتنهض بها. قاله أبو عبيد

rows.speaker: بديل بن ميسرة
rows.claim: Budayl ibn Maysara reads yanūʾu with masculine agreement because he supplies the omitted noun ḥamluhā or thiqluhā as the subject.
rows.anchor: وقرأ بديل بن ميسرة " لينوء " بالياء

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī also suggests the pronoun in mafātiḥuhu refers to Qārūn, with mafātiḥ acquiring masculine agreement from its genitive complement.
rows.anchor: وقيل: الضمير في " مفاتحه " لقارون، فاكتسب المضاف من المضاف إليه التذكير كقولهم: " ذهبت أهل اليمامة " قاله الزمخشري
